hints: Start from the monomer of PVC, chloroethene, and think about what happens to its C=C double bond during addition polymerisation.
The monomer is $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$, so opening the double bond gives a two-carbon unit with only one Cl still attached.
Compare that real repeat unit with the one quoted in the question and check which statement cannot be true.
walkthrough:
**Recall the monomer of PVC**

PVC is poly(chloroethene), commonly called poly(vinyl chloride). Its monomer is chloroethene.

$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$$

**Form the true repeat unit**

In addition polymerisation the C=C double bond opens to form two new C-C single bonds. Each monomer therefore becomes a saturated unit.

$$n\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl} \rightarrow \text{-(CH}_2\text{-CHCl)-}_n$$

**Test each statement**

Combustion of a Cl-containing polymer gives $\text{HCl}$ gas, which is highly acidic. The polymer is saturated because the double bond is lost, and addition polymerisation does not change the empirical formula, so $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl}$ is kept. The only statement that does not match is the repeat unit with two Cl atoms.

options.A: This is a correct statement, so it is not the answer. PVC contains chlorine, so burning it produces hydrogen chloride, $\text{HCl}$, which dissolves to give a strongly acidic gas and solution.
options.B: This is a correct statement, so it is not the answer. PVC is an addition polymer, the C=C of the monomer is converted to C-C single bonds, so the long chain contains only single bonds and is saturated.
options.C: This is a correct statement, so it is not the answer. Addition polymerisation just joins monomers with no small molecule lost, so polymer $(\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl})_n$ has the same empirical formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl}$ as the monomer.
options.D: This is the not correct statement, so it is the answer. The true repeat unit is $\text{-(CH}_2\text{-CHCl)-}$ with only one Cl per two carbons. The quoted $\text{-(CHCl-CHCl)-}$ would need two Cl atoms per monomer, which is wrong.
